correction: docs/org-adrs.md recorded that snapshot.yml dispatches build to frostyard/snow (core ADR-0013). frostyard/snow had been renamed frostyard/snow-bootc, archived and marked Deprecated, and the continue-on-error 'Kickoff snow' step failed on every snapshot run checked (2026-08-19 to 2026-09-28) without failing the workflow. Image rebuilds are now dispatched by frostyard/apt-publisher after a tag release is published (core ADR-0056), and snapshot.yml dispatches nothing.
evidence: gh repo view frostyard/snow (name snow-bootc, archived, 'Deprecated'); 'Kickoff snow' step errors in snapshot runs 32284872244, 33163172585, 34913816701, 36475121875 and 36478845492; frostyard/core ADR-0056

correction: AGENTS.md documented `make test` as running `go test ./...`, and the frostyard-go-repo skill documents `make bump` as running build/test/fmt/lint before tagging. `test` was missing from `.PHONY`, so make treated the target as the top-level `test/` directory, reported it up to date and ran nothing; `make bump` tagged v0.11.2 without running the tests. Every Makefile target is now declared `.PHONY`, and a test enforces it.
evidence: `make test` on 3505e94 printed "make: 'test' is up to date." and exited 0; `make bump` printed "make[1]: 'test' is up to date." while tagging v0.11.2; internal/installcheck/makefile_phony_test.go

correction: ChairLift assumed that a nil error from updex Client.UpdateFeatures meant every enabled feature updated, and always showed 'Features updated. Changes apply after reboot.'. Since updex v2.1.0 a nil error also covers features the next-boot image gate holds (transfer NeedsImage or NotLinked, Installed=false) and features held by a rollback record. updex v2.1.3 can also return an error wrapping sysext.ErrActivationIncomplete (merged, activation unfinished), and a per-transfer failure returns the results together with the error. Only the per-feature results say what happened.
evidence: github.com/frostyard/updex/v2@v2.1.3 updex/features.go UpdateFeatures (NeedsImage/NotLinked/Held branches, 'return allResults, errors.Join(...)'), updex/results.go UpdateResult, sysext/runner.go ErrActivationIncomplete; chairlift PR #253

correction: ChairLift believed the unprivileged Features update check reported NeedsImage on bootc hosts. Reality: bootc status --json needs root, so updex's minimum image version gate erred on every component, and ChairLift's partitionFeatureChecks dropped those components, so the 'waiting for a newer OS image' row never appeared after a restart on a bootc host.
evidence: bootc status --json as uid 1001 on bootc 1.17.1 prints 'This command must be executed as the root user'; updex v2.1.3 imagecompat/bootc.go NextBootImageVersion falls back only on exec.ErrNotFound; internal/updex/partitionFeatureChecks drops component errors

correction: PR #261 believed the danglingSymlink check in Load made every dangling config symlink fail closed. Reality: resolveCandidatePath probed the executable-relative config.yml with os.Stat, so a dangling symlink there resolved to the working-directory file instead and Load fell through to it or to enabled defaults. The probe is now os.Lstat.
evidence: cross-review of frostyard/chairlift#261 at 471d36e5; internal/config.TestLoadDanglingExecutableRelativeSymlinkFailsClosed and the dangling subtest of TestResolveCandidatePathBranches fail with statPath = os.Stat

correction: PR #260 disabled Pango markup on toasts but no test guarded it: with window.go reverted, every test still passed. The change was unprotected because internal/window cannot host a test binary.
evidence: cross-review of frostyard/chairlift#260 at 6e51495e; internal/installcheck.TestToastsRenderPlainText now parses production Go files and fails when an adw.NewToast result is shown without SetUseMarkup(false)

correction: ChairLift believed a nil error from updex Client.Features meant updex features were configured, so updex.IsInstalled returned true on a host without feature definitions and the Features page showed an empty group with an active Update button. updex returns an empty slice with a nil error when no features are configured; IsInstalled now also requires len(features) > 0.
evidence: github.com/frostyard/updex/v2@v2.1.3 updex/features.go Client.Features ('if len(features) == 0 { ... return []FeatureInfo{}, nil }'); internal/updex.TestUpdexAvailabilityRequiresNonEmptyFeatures; ported from the bluefin chairlift fork (0f069c8e)

correction: PR #262 believed a scope-less `flatpak uninstall --unused` cleaned only the system installation and split it into --user and --system runs. Reality: flatpak parses uninstall with FLATPAK_BUILTIN_FLAG_ALL_DIRS, so the scope-less command already cleans the user, the default system and every extra system installation; the split dropped the extra installations.
evidence: flatpak app/flatpak-builtins-uninstall.c (ALL_DIRS flag, --unused loop over dirs) and app/flatpak-main.c (no scope flag selects user, system and installations.d dirs), tags 1.10.0, 1.14.0, 1.16.0; internal/flatpak.TestUninstallUnusedCoversEveryInstallation

correction: PR #262 believed the Flatpak update reload would always replace the clicked row, so the per-app button stayed at 'Updating...' after success. Reality: a reload in which both installation queries fail keeps the old rows, so the button stuck. The button now follows actionstate.PackageUpgrade: restore on failure or dry-run, remove the row and decrement the count on live success.
evidence: cross-review of frostyard/chairlift#262 at 0cde3b64; internal/views/actionstate.TestUpdatesPageRetiresCompletedFlatpakUpdateRows

correction: ChairLift treated a RemoteError from both Flatpak installations as a total failure even when each query returned healthy-remotes updates. Partial updates are now authoritative and publishable; only two failed installations with zero updates keep the last known rows and count.
evidence: issue #263; internal/views/flatpakstatus/flatpakstatus.go; internal/views/flatpakstatus/flatpakstatus_test.go TestBothInstallationsPartialPublishesHealthyUpdates

correction: PR #265 believed the Progress worker could run on its own after the window closed. Reality: the worker had no application hold and no close guard, so a close ended ChairLift while flatpak still ran and the completion markers were never written. The window now blocks close-request while Flow.CanClose is false and holds the application until the worker ends.
evidence: PR #265 cross-review; internal/firstrun.TestFlowCanClose and TestWindowGuardsCloseDuringProgress

correction: PR #265 believed a logged completion failure was enough. Reality: a ResolvePaths or MarkDone error left the Done step saying 'Your user account is ready to use'. Completion now carries Err and ShowWarning, and DoneState shows the warning and an error-log entry. The 'starts again at your next login' text shows only when no marker exists after the failure (DoneAt is false); a partial failure that left a marker shows 'Setup finished with errors'.
evidence: PR #265 cross-review and re-review 1; internal/firstrun.TestCompleteReportsMarkDoneFailure, TestCompleteAtReportsMissingConfigHome and TestCompletePartialFailureDoesNotPromiseAnotherRun

correction: PR #265 believed one gsettings goroutine per Style toggle was safe. Reality: the goroutines can finish out of order and leave the color scheme the user did not choose last. One SchemeWriter now writes serially and the latest choice wins.
evidence: PR #265 cross-review; internal/firstrun.TestSchemeWriterLatestChoiceWins and TestWindowWritesColorSchemeSerially

correction: PR #265 believed logging a configuration error was enough in the first-run window. Reality: AGENTS.md requires a configuration error to stay visible as a persistent toast. The first-run window now shows LoadError.ToastMessage in a toast with timeout 0 and markup off.
evidence: PR #265 cross-review; internal/firstrun.TestWindowShowsConfigErrorToast and internal/installcheck.TestToastsRenderPlainText

correction: PR #265 believed a 0700 mode check on the config home proved MarkDone's directory mode. Reality: the test pre-created the config home with touch (0755), so the check passed only under a 077 umask and failed in CI (umask 022). The mode check now uses a fresh config home that only MarkDone creates, and the legacy autostart removal has its own test.
evidence: PR #265 CI (Unit Tests, Race Detection) at 60c7a28; internal/firstrun.TestMarkDoneWritesBothMarkersInPrivateDirectories and TestMarkDoneRemovesLegacyAutostart, run under umask 022 and 077

correction: PR #265 believed the serial SchemeWriter alone kept the last color-scheme choice. Reality: nothing drained it, so Progress could record completion, release the hold and show Exit while a write was pending, and Exit ended the process first. RunProgress now runs the actions, drains the writer (SchemeWriter.Wait), then records completion, on the worker goroutine.
evidence: PR #265 re-review 1; internal/firstrun.TestRunProgressDrainsSchemeWriterBeforeCompletion and TestWindowDrainsSchemeWriterBeforeCompletion

correction: PR #265 believed every completion error meant the first run starts again at the next login. Reality: MarkDone can fail after it wrote the markers (for example when the legacy autostart path is a non-empty directory), and the gate then skips the next login. DoneState now takes the gate state (DoneAt) and shows 'starts again' only when no marker exists, else 'Setup finished with errors'.
evidence: PR #265 re-review 1; internal/firstrun.TestCompletePartialFailureDoesNotPromiseAnotherRun and TestDoneState

correction: PR #265 believed 'not done' after a completion failure meant the gate starts the first run again. Reality: with no config home the window's DoneAt was false too, but the gate in that environment exits 1 and starts nothing, so 'starts again at your next login' was false. DoneState now takes a 3-state GateState (GateRunsAgain, GateDone, GateUnknown) from GateStateAt and promises another run only for GateRunsAgain; GateUnknown is the zero value.
evidence: PR #265 re-review 2; internal/firstrun.TestCompleteAtReportsMissingConfigHome, TestDoneState and TestGateStateAt

correction: The Problems page (T857 t6) believed std v0.4.0 problems.Read with Limit 500 bounded the journal read. Reality: Read keeps all journalctl stdout and stderr in unbounded bytes.Buffer values, and 500 entries do not bound bytes, so a forged entry with a huge field could exhaust memory. ChairLift now runs journalctl itself with Read's arguments (problems.JournalArgs), reads at most 8 MiB of stdout and 4 KiB of stderr, kills journalctl at the cap, parses only the complete lines before it with problems.ParseJSON, and logs the truncation; the coredumpctl read stops and kills at its 4 MiB cap too.
evidence: cross-review of the T857 t6 change; github.com/frostyard/std@v0.4.0 problems/read_linux.go Read (bytes.Buffer stdout/stderr); internal/problems.TestJournalReadIsCapped and TestCoredumpReadIsCapped

correction: The Problems page (T857 t6) believed decoding a v1 integer field into json.Number checked its JSON type. Reality: json.Number also accepts a JSON string of digits, so "retries": "1" passed and the item became reportable. An integer field now must be a JSON number token (decodeNumber); other numbers and booleans decode into Go int, int64 or bool, which reject JSON text.
evidence: cross-review of the T857 t6 change; internal/problems.TestForgedValuesAreShownButNotReportable (retries as text), TestQuotedNumbersAndBooleansAreNotTrusted and TestDecodeNumber

correction: The capped command reads of the Problems page (T857 t6) believed killing the command process at the cap was enough. Reality: a descendant that inherited stdout or stderr kept the pipes open, so cmd.Wait blocked forever (WaitDelay was zero, and the context deadline does not close inherited pipes). execStream now starts the command in its own process group, kills the whole group at the cap and on context cancel (cmd.Cancel), closes the parent's stdout reader before Wait, calls Wait once, and sets WaitDelay to 2 seconds.
evidence: re-review 1 of the T857 t6 change; internal/problems.TestCappedReadKillsDescendantsThatHoldThePipes times out without the group kill and WaitDelay

correction: The opt-in reporting sender (T857 t19) believed reading the consent once per run, and once before the pace wait, was enough, and that asynchronous consent writes were safe. Reality: a withdrawal by another ChairLift process during the pace, or between the reservation save and the request, could still send, and a queued consent write could restore an older value or lose an Off. The consent is now read again after the pace and again after the reservation save, just before the request (a withdrawal rolls the reservation back and stops without a pause), the page and the first run write the small consent file synchronously on the main thread with 1 in-memory authority, and a live send reloads the consent file before every request (reporting.FileConsent).
evidence: re-review 1 of the T857 t19 change (frostyard/chairlift#267); internal/reporting TestRunWithdrawDuringThePaceStopsTheNextRequest (fails with 4 saves when the post-pace check is removed), TestRunWithdrawAfterTheReservationStopsTheRequest, TestSendReportWithdrawAfterTheReservationSendsNothing, TestFileConsentReloads, TestRunFailedRollbackSaveKeepsTheReservation

correction: The T857 t19 live consent gate believed Stricter(memory, file) covered a local withdrawal during a send. Reality: Go evaluates memory first, so a withdrawal made while the file read blocked was lost and both values read On. reporting.LiveConsent now reads the file first, then memory. The load guard and the dry-run Auto preview of the page had only helper tests; source guards now pin their wiring.
evidence: re-review 3 of chairlift#267 (P1, P2); internal/reporting.TestLiveConsentReadsTheFileFirst fails with the old order; internal/installcheck.TestLiveSendsUseTheFileFirstGate, TestReportingControlsWaitForTheFirstLoad, TestDryRunAutoChoiceStartsThePreviewRun

correction: The baseline PR #272 carried two .planning/CONCERNS.md facts as checked: that launchApp receives application IDs from Flatpak and desktop-file listings, and that maintenance runs are not logged beyond an error toast. Reality: both launchApp callers take the ID from configuration (applications_installed_group and health_group app_id, with Bazaar and Mission Center defaults), and runMaintenanceAction logs the title, script and sudo value when a run starts; it discards the script output and logs no result.
evidence: cross-review of frostyard/chairlift#272 at 964bf91; internal/views/applications_page.go:44-51, internal/views/system_page.go:72-79, internal/views/maintenance_page.go:213-214

correction: PR #272 at 964bf91 believed that git cat-file -e BASE:scripts/check-corrections.mjs failing meant BASE predates the corrections gate. Reality: it also fails when BASE does not resolve (a typo or an unfetched ref), so make ci skipped the append-only comparison and passed. corrections-base now requires BASE to resolve to a commit first.
evidence: cross-review of frostyard/chairlift#272 at 964bf91; internal/installcheck.TestCorrectionsBaseRejectsUnresolvableBase fails with the old single cat-file form

correction: Sync PR #273 was believed safe to merge because its checks were green. Reality: its branch was cut while .agents was a symlink to docs/agents, so the sync wrote frostyard-readme to docs/agents/skills/. PR #272 made .agents a real directory before #273 merged, and the merge left the skill outside .agents/skills/; the docs-index gate then failed on main. The skill now lives in .agents/skills/, and a test pins that every synced skill lives there.
evidence: Tests run 42203927812 (Verify, FAIL docs-index: docs/agents/skills/frostyard-readme/SKILL.md); internal/installcheck.TestSyncedSkillsLiveInAgentsSkills fails with the old layout

correction: docs/design/overview.md's bootc boot gate section believed that running bootc status --format json unprivileged and checking status.booted detects every snow bootc host. Reality: the bootc on current Snow answers status only as root ('This command must be executed as the root user'), so IsBootcBootedCached is false on a Snow bootc host and the deployment chain and the image source stayed hidden. The snosi stager records the image, the running and remote versions and the staged digest in /run/snosi on bootc hosts too; System now reads them there when status is refused.
evidence: bootc status --format json on a Snow bootc host (2026-11-10) printed the root-only error; /run/snosi/update-check held image=ghcr.io/frostyard/snow:latest, running_version and remote_version; internal/views.TestSystemReadsBootcFromSnosiWhenStatusNeedsRoot

correction: The lint gate believed golangci-lint must be built with a Go no older than go.mod's full go line (patch included). Reality: gofmt and the typechecker follow the language version (MAJOR.MINOR); golangci-lint 2.15.0 built with go1.27.0 lints the go 1.27.3 module (raised by MyGo) with 0 issues. The gate compares MAJOR.MINOR now.
evidence: CGO_ENABLED=0 golangci-lint run with the mise-pinned 2.15.0 (built with go1.27.0) on feat/mygo: 0 issues
